<!-- TODO: rewrite this paragraph in your own words. Keep it to 2–3 sentences. -->
I am interested in how quantitative imaging can capture the biological organisation of tumours, and how imaging, molecular and spatial data can be integrated into clinically meaningful cancer phenotypes.

<!-- TODO: one short paragraph connecting where you've been (SPARK, transcriptomic modules) to where you're going (imaging). -->
My background is in transcriptomics and prognostic modelling. I now ask whether the biology those molecular programmes describe is visible in medical images, and what imaging can reveal that a biopsy cannot.

## Current questions

<!-- TODO: 2–4 questions you are actually thinking about right now. Update these often. -->

- What does radiomic "heterogeneity" actually measure?
- Does the tissue just outside a tumour carry information that tumour-only imaging misses?
- Where are stromal, immune and tumour programmes located relative to one another?

## Trajectory

::: {.trajectory}
Transcriptomic modules → Cancer imaging → Radiomics → Radiogenomics → Peritumoural imaging → Spatial tumour biology → Multimodal precision oncology
:::
